title: Hide Delegate

solutions.title: One loanLimit() query, not a chain
solutions.tradeoff: Two one-line forwarding methods - one on Membership, one on Member - and Membership.tier() no longer has a public caller anywhere, so a future feature that needs the tier for something other than its loan limit has to add an accessor back, not find one waiting.

reviewFocus: Count the call sites this fixes against the methods it adds: six `member.membership().tier().loanLimit()` chains collapsed by two forwarding methods. Does the walkthrough make that count explicit, or just assert the refactoring is worth it?
Is `Membership.tier()` still public anywhere, or does the compiler now refuse any code that tries to reach past `Member.loanLimit()`?

Does `Member.loanLimit()` call `this.#membership.loanLimit()`, or does it reach two levels down to `this.#membership.tier().loanLimit()` directly - skipping Membership's own hide and leaving half the chain exposed?

Compare against drill-07-08: both touch a forwarding method, in opposite directions. Does this walkthrough's reasoning for hiding actually fail the test drill-07-08 applies to Branch, or does it hold up?
Is `totalBranchLoanCapacity` still summing `loanLimit()` once per member, or did collapsing the chain quietly change what it computes?
